parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State how, in a modern X-ray tube, the intensity of the X-ray beam and its hardness are controlled.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
A model of a limb consists of soft tissue and bone, as illustrated in Fig. 11.1.

{{figure:figure_11_1.png}}

The soft tissue has a thickness of $9.0\text{ cm}$. The bone within the soft tissue has a thickness of $3.0\text{ cm}$.

Data for the linear attenuation (absorption) coefficient $\mu$ of X-rays in soft tissue and in bone are shown in Table 11.1.

Table 11.1

| {{blank}} | {{header}} $\mu / \text{cm}^{-1}$ |
| soft tissue | 0.92 |
| bone | 2.9 |

A parallel beam of X-rays of intensity $I_0$ is incident normally on the model.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: the transmitted intensity $I_{\text{S}}$ through soft tissue alone

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: the transmitted intensity $I_{\text{C}}$ through soft tissue and bone.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: By reference to your answers in (b), suggest, with a reason, whether good contrast on an X-ray image would be obtained.
